subject: chemistry
title: Covalent bonding and dot-and-cross diagrams
key_idea: A covalent bond is a shared pair of electrons between two atoms. It forms between non-metal atoms and the bond is strong. Atoms joined by covalent bonds make molecules, and dot and cross diagrams show the shared electrons.

blocks.text: Non-metal atoms share electrons to fill their outer shells. This section covers what a covalent bond and a molecule are.

items.meaning: A shared pair of electrons between two atoms.
Two or more atoms joined together by covalent bonds.
One, two or three shared pairs between the same two atoms.

items: Covalent bonding occurs in most non-metal elements and in compounds of non-metals.
The bonds between atoms are strong.
Covalent bonding is sharing. Ionic bonding is transfer.
Some covalent substances are small molecules. Others are polymers or giant structures.

items: A covalent bond is a shared pair of electrons between non-metal atoms.
A molecule is two or more atoms joined by covalent bonds.
Double and triple bonds are two or three shared pairs.

blocks.text: A dot and cross diagram shows only the outer-shell electrons. The dots and crosses represent the electrons of the different atoms.

items.text: Draw the outer shell of each atom, overlapping where they join.
Use dots for one atom's electrons and crosses for the other's.
Put one dot and one cross in the overlap for each shared pair. Each pair is one covalent bond, so a double bond has two pairs.
Add the other electrons until every atom has a full outer shell.

blocks.text: Hydrogen needs two electrons to fill its shell. In water, each hydrogen shares one pair with oxygen, and oxygen has two shared pairs.
Other ways to show a molecule

items: A line between symbols shows a single bond, as in H–Cl.
A molecular formula, such as NH₃, can be worked out by counting the atoms in a diagram or model.
A polymer is drawn as its repeating unit in brackets, with n outside to show that n is a large number.
A small molecule has a few atoms. A polymer has very long molecules. A giant structure continues in all directions.
Phosphorus is in the same group as nitrogen, so with hydrogen it makes PH₃, like NH₃.

rows: Does not show the shape of the molecule, and is only two-dimensional
Not to scale, so the size of atoms is wrong, and the atoms are shown separated
Does not show the electrons or shells

items: Dots and crosses are electrons, drawn only for the outer shell.
The overlap of two shells holds the shared pairs between those two atoms.
Dot and cross diagrams do not show shape. Ball and stick models do not show electrons.

checks.a: Two, which is a double bond.

worked_example.question: Explain why water (H₂O) has a low melting point.
answer_points: Water is made of small molecules, or simple molecules.
With weak forces between the molecules, the intermolecular forces.
So little energy is needed to overcome the intermolecular forces and separate the molecules.
worked_example.tip: Do not write about breaking covalent bonds. The covalent bonds inside each molecule stay in place.

worked_example.question: Chlorine exists as diatomic molecules. In a molecule, two chlorine atoms are joined by a covalent bond. Describe what is meant by a covalent bond.
answer_points: A pair of electrons, two electrons.
worked_example.tip: A diagram can earn both marks. Any reference to ionic bonding or ions scores zero.

worked_example.question: Plastics are polymers. Polymers have covalent bonds between the atoms. Explain what a covalent bond is in terms of electrons.
answer_points: A covalent bond is a shared pair of electrons between atoms.
worked_example.tip: One mark for the idea of a shared pair.

worked_example.question: This question is about covalent compounds. State what is meant by a covalent bond.
worked_example.tip: One mark for the pair of electrons and one for sharing between two atoms.

items: In a covalent bond each atom ends up with a noble gas electronic structure.
Hydrogen has two electrons in its shell, like helium.

worked_example.question: Hydrogen chloride is a covalent compound. State, in terms of electrostatic attraction, what is meant by a covalent bond.
answer_points: Electrostatic attraction between the nuclei of both atoms.
And a shared (bonding) pair of electrons.
worked_example.tip: Write nuclei, in the plural. The attraction is between the shared pair and the nuclei of both atoms.

items.meaning: The smallest part of an element that can take part in a chemical reaction.

blocks.text: A covalent bond is the electrostatic attraction between the nuclei of both atoms and the shared pair of electrons between them.
